newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM reshuffles cabinet, appoints assistant.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM reshuffles cabinet, appoints assistant.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson announced some limited changes to his cabinet on Tuesday, effectively appointing veteran politician Thage Peterson his deputy.
After a hastily called cabinet meeting, Persson said Defence Minister Peterson would become a member of the inner cabinet which comprises his close group of advisers.
He will be replaced by Industry and Commerce Minister Bjorn von Sydow while junior cabinet minister to the Prime Minister's office Leif Pagrotsky will take over from von Sydow.
The changes take effect from February 1.

"Peterson made it clear in March (1996) when he started as defence minister that he wanted to leave the government after the (domestic) defence agreement (in parliament) was settled," Persson told a news conference.
"But I do not want him to quit the inner cabinet as he has so much experience and knowledge."
Persson said Peterson, a heavyweight in the ruling Social Democrats, will assist him as he prepares for the next general election in September 1998.
There has been no deputy prime minister in Sweden since the end of 1995 when Mona Sahlin was pushed out of office after allegations that she had misused a government credit card.
Peterson is seen as one of Sweden's most experienced politicians and was a member of the inner cabinet of former Prime Minister Olof Palme, who was shot dead in a Stockholm street in February 1986.
"His task will be to assist and help me, mainly with the duties regarding parliament and the (Social Democratic) parliamentary group when I do not have time," Persson said.
Persson said Peterson will also look at reforming budget cutbacks which have not had the desired effects.
"We must be self critical," Peterson later told reporters.
"We have agreed on many painful cutbacks that have been rough on many people. An important goal is to win the general election in 1998."
The cabinet changes were the first made by Persson since he took over the leadership of the Social Democrats in March 1986 and became prime minister.
He replaced Ingvar Carlsson, who retired.
Announcing the changes, Persson said Pagrotsky, one of his close allies, will retain his weapon export portfolio when he becomes Industry and Commerce Minister.
"Leif Pagrotsky and I will sit down and discuss if these tasks can be combined," Persson said.
